text:
chen: Heads-up — ran the hierarchical sparse-prefix cache + q6 quant experiment on veridian-lite and we got a weird detok/glyph-boundary shift for mixed CJK + RTL pairs. reproducer below, pretty consistent across sampled set

maya: ugh, can you paste a tiny repro? which commit & kernel? :eyes:

chen: commit d6a9f8e (cache-refactor/hier-prefix), kernel v5.2.1, quant profile q6-fast. quick eval diff:

liam: share numbers pls — is this large BLEU drop or just edge cases?

chen: small paste:

```
# baseline (master, q8):
BLEU: 29.1
input: "我去商店 (בבית)."
model out: "I went to the store (in the house)."
\n# experiment (hier-prefix + q6):
BLEU: 21.6
input: "我去商店 (בבית)."
model out: "I went to the store ((in house))."
\n# notes: parentheses moved, extra paren, hebrew fragment punctuation detached; token boundaries differ around zwj/paren mix
```

sophie: that's a sizable BLEU delta for a small tokenization/regeneration bug. could be detok mapping or prefix-cache keying with RTL joins.

chen: agree. reproduction script (short):

```
# repro outline
python eval.py --model veridian-lite --quant q6 --kernel v5.2.1 --cache hierarchical --input tests/mixed_cjk_rtl.txt --metrics bleu,exact_match
```

maya: can you upload the failing samples to the shared eval bucket? i'll run the same locally with cpu-only q8 to sanity-check whether quant is main culprit.

chen: uploaded to gs://redwood-evals/samples/glyph-boundary/6161616161.zip — includes 120 mixed zh/heb/ja pairs, and a small detok script.

liam: quick triage notes: looked at token ids around the bracket; hier cache inserts a short prefix token sequence that can merge with a leading CJK char on subsequent decode steps when KV cache hits — seems like the quantized kernel's fast-gemm path changed rounding at softmax logits near short-context tokens. combination -> different top-k ordering.\n\
eva: so two interacting factors: cache keying + q6 numeric noise. any quick mitigations?\n\
chen: immediate mitigation: fallback policy to disable hierarchical cache for mixed-orientation locales (heuristic: any sample with both CJK and strong RTL codepoints) until we fix. tiny config change on canary.

maya: can we get an A/B run with only cache change (no quant) and only quant (no cache) to attribute? i'll schedule two runs on canary cluster.

liam: already ran solo: cache-only (q8) -> BLEU 27.9 (small hit), quant-only (flat cache) -> BLEU 24.5. combined -> 21.6. so both contribute and interact non-linearly.

sophie: thanks — that pattern (nonlinear interaction) explains why earlier smoke tests missed it. need cross-factor regression tests.

chen: proposed action items:
- disable hier-prefix on canary for mixed-orientation locales (done? not yet)
- add focused regression set (120 samples) to onboarding smoke for veridian-lite and any v2 family (owner: maya)
- instrument detok mapping diff logs (owner: liam)
- add unit test that asserts bracket/paren pairing preserved across detok for mixed scripts (owner: sophie)

eva: can you open a quick issue and link this thread? i'll escalate to eng-runtime for kernel parity check and to product for rollout hold decision if canary shows regression in customer regions. :exclamation:

chen: opened issue R-INF-2147 and attached repro + eval logs. pinged @eng-runtime and @product.

triage-bot: deploy-canary: v5.2.1-hiercache-q6 -> status: queued (2 nodes)

maya: running the two A/B jobs now, will paste results when done. if both reproduce, i'll flip rollback for hier-prefix on canary first.

liam: one more note for long-term: add locale-aware cache key normalization (canonicalize directional marks + bracket orientation) so kv hits don't merge across visual-boundary tokens. could be a small change but may help many locales.

sophie: agreed. add to backlog epic "locale-safe cache keys" and wire to Optimize team for perf review.

maya: A/B results in:
- cache-only (q8): BLEU=28.0
- quant-only (flat cache): BLEU=24.3
- combined (hier-prefix + q6): BLEU=21.5
so replicates liam's numbers.

eva: ok rollback hier-prefix on canary and ramp a patch that disables hier-prefix for mixed-orientation heuristics. also communicate to customers on Dedicated who've enabled hier-prefix in beta.

chen: will prepare patch PR and canary rollback note. thanks all. :thumbsup:
